title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. L is a function field of transcendence degree n over a base field K. L-bar is an algebraic (separable) closure of L, and E_L^{L-bar} = Gal(L-bar/L). For a normal model U of L (a variety over K with function field L), E_U^{L-bar} denotes the profinite fundamental group pi_1(U, L-bar), which is a quotient of Gal(L-bar/L). The previous page showed the following. For a valuation V with centre x' and inertia group I_{x'}, the composite I_{x'} -> E_U is trivial when the valuation has a centre on U. That is, the map E_{U~_x} -> E_U factors through the strict henselisation.

First paragraph (end of the argument). E_U^{L-bar} is recovered from Gal(L-bar/L) in three steps:
- Take the valuation rings V = O_{U,x}, for x running over the codimension-1 points of U. These are the divisorial valuations with centre on U.
- Take the closed normal subgroup generated by their inertia groups I_V.
- Divide Gal(L-bar/L) by that subgroup: pi_1(U) = Gal(L-bar/L) / <<I_V : V = O_{U,x}, codim x = 1>>.
This is the Galois-theoretic form of 'finite etale = unramified in codimension 1', i.e. Zariski–Nagata purity of the branch locus. It is the starting point for reading pi_1 of models off decomposition and inertia data in the absolute Galois group. That is a central theme of the Longue Marche: birational/anabelian reconstruction of models and valuations from Galois data.

Second part. He introduces the locally ringed space X_{L/K} = projective limit of all proper models X of L/K. This is the Zariski–Riemann space ('abstract Riemann surface') of L/K. He notes:
- It is not a scheme if n >= 2.
- For a point x, the residue field k(x) is an extension of K of transcendence degree d <= n, and n - d plays the role of codimension (d is the 'dimension' of x).
- There is a unique point of codimension 0, lying over the generic points of the models.
- The marginal NB worries that the definition depends on resolution of singularities (reference '(31)') unless singular models are allowed.

Next page. Codimension-1 points correspond to the divisorial valuations, i.e. 'the V above'. He then states and proves (via resolution and monomialisation of f = g/h) Zariski's theorem: x -> O_{X,x} is a bijection from the Zariski–Riemann space onto the set of valuation rings of L containing K.
errors: The quotient description gives exactly pi_1(U) only under purity of the branch locus, i.e. for U regular (Zariski–Nagata, SGA1 X / SGA2 X). For a merely normal U, the quotient by inertia of codimension-1 points classifies covers unramified in codimension 1, which can be larger than pi_1(U). Example: a quotient singularity has nontrivial covers unramified in codimension 1 that are not etale. Grothendieck's surrounding context presumably assumes regular models.

The marginal concern about dependence on resolution is unnecessary for the definition. The projective limit over all proper (possibly singular) models is well defined in any characteristic. Zariski's bijection theorem also does not need resolution: blow up the ideal (g,h) to make it invertible, so that f or 1/f becomes regular at the centre. The proof on the next page via monomialisation is therefore overkill and restricts the argument to characteristic 0 (or low dimension).

The 'codimension = n - d' bookkeeping is only heuristic. In the Zariski–Riemann space, transcendence degree of the residue field does not determine the height/rank of the valuation, nor topological codimension.

Related claim on the next page ('sauf erreur'): that only codimension-0 and codimension-1 points have noetherian local rings. This is false for n >= 2. There are non-divisorial discrete rank-1 valuations whose local rings are DVRs. Example: f(x,y) -> ord_t f(t, e^t) on K(x,y), with residue field K, so d = 0.

ideas.what: pi_1 of a (regular) model U as the quotient of Gal(L-bar/L) by the closed normal subgroup generated by the inertia groups of the divisorial valuations centred on U
ideas.modern_name: Purity of the branch locus / Galois description of the etale fundamental group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Zariski–Nagata (purity); Grothendieck SGA1 V and X, SGA2

ideas.what: The limit of all proper models as a locally ringed space, not a scheme for n >= 2, with points corresponding to the valuation rings of L/K
ideas.modern_name: Zariski–Riemann space (Riemann–Zariski space) as the projective limit of models
ideas.usually_credited_to: Zariski (1940s); limit-of-models formulation in EGA-style language and later by Temkin, Huber (adic spaces)
ideas.where_published: Brief mentions in Longue Marche material; not in EGA as such (unsure)

ideas.what: Codimension-1 points of the Zariski–Riemann space as the divisorial valuations, the ones whose inertia is used for the fundamental groups of models
ideas.modern_name: Divisorial valuations / divisorial inertia in birational anabelian geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Zariski); in the Galois setting Pop, Bogomolov–Tschinkel (1990s–2000s)
ideas.where_published: Theme of La Longue Marche (1981 manuscript), partially published (unsure)

missed.claim: Grothendieck combines the Zariski–Riemann space with Galois inertia: all pi_1 of models are obtained as quotients of Gal(L-bar/L) by inertia of divisorial points of the Zariski–Riemann space. This prefigures later birational anabelian approaches (Pop's recovery of divisorial/quasi-divisorial valuations from Galois groups) and the use of Riemann–Zariski spaces in etale homotopy of function fields. The idea itself is well known today, so this is a historical precedence note rather than a new result.
missed.quote: on prend les V = O_{U,x}, où x est un pt de codim 1 dans U ... en divisant par le sous-groupe fermé invariant engendré par les I_V
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that already in 1981 Grothendieck framed birational anabelian reconstruction via the Zariski–Riemann space and divisorial inertia. Mostly of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is standard: purity-based description of pi_1 and Zariski's Riemann space and valuation bijection. Its interest is historical, linking the Riemann–Zariski space to Galois inertia in the Longue Marche. A minor false 'sauf erreur' claim follows on the next page.
transcription_corrections: 'E_U^L' and 'E_L^L' should read \mathcal{E}_U^{\bar L} and \mathcal{E}_L^{\bar L}.
'tous les V dans L correspondant aux centres sur U (i.e. infinis[?])': the parenthesis is hard to read; probably '(i.e. ayant un centre sur U)' or similar, uncertain.
'lim des modèles (singuliers) propres plats[?] L sur K': likely 'propres de L sur K'; 'plats' is doubtful.
'Les x ∈ 𝒳, k(x)...' probably 'Pour x ∈ 𝒳, k(x) est une ext. de K de degré de transcendance d ≤ n; n − d est la codim., d la dimension de x'.
'Il y a un pt et un seul de codim 0, correspondant aux pts gén. des X'.
